clue.text: Beast takes space traveller round

parts.note: a bull is a large horned beast
ET, the extraterrestrial of the film, travelled through space

explanation.surface: An animal gives a lift to a visitor from outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: A round is a single piece of ammunition fired from a gun, a cartridge or projectile.

clue.text: The Spanish don't allow cattle: one up to the steadfast in mind

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading upwards means the whole string of pieces is turned backwards

parts.note: el is the Spanish for 'the'
to bar is to prohibit
oxen are cattle
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Spaniard bans cattle, which only the resolute would attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole run EL BAR OXEN I backwards, giving the answer from the bottom of the light upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inexorable cannot be moved by pleading, so they are unshakeably steadfast in purpose.

clue.text: Second in contest for most of school time: needs periodic reading

indicators.note: the letter for a second is put inside the word for a contest

parts.note: a game is a contest

indicators.note: all of the word but its last letter is used

parts.note: a term is a period of the school year

explanation.surface: A runner-up in a school contest during term time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of TERM to leave TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas meter must be read by the supplier at regular intervals to bill the customer.

clue.text: Shelter in the trench from the French disease

parts.note: du is French for 'from the' (of the)
gout is a disease of the joints

explanation.surface: A soldier in the trenches seeks shelter from a French illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A dugout is a roofed refuge dug into the side of a trench, as in the First World War.

clue.text: Pickpockets take credit for assessing lubricant

parts.note: a dip is slang for a pickpocket
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: Thieves buy on credit at the garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for 'on credit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dipstick is the rod pushed into an engine's sump to measure the oil level.

clue.text: Gadabout been left inside is seen from the side of the house

definitions.text: seen from the side of the house

indicators.note: the 'about' of Gadabout says the word gad goes round the rest

parts.note: to gad is to roam about

indicators.note: the letter for left is put inside the word been

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wanderer who has been left indoors looks out of the side of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gadabout' looks like one word for a wanderer, but split it: its tail 'about' is the container signal, and 'inside' puts L within BEEN to make BLEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gable end is the triangular wall at the side of a pitched-roof house, visible in side view.

clue.text: Lulu with fan may be offending

indicators.note: the words may be rearranged into another form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lulu the pop singer with an admirer could be breaking the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' signals an anagram of LULU, W and FAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlawful offends against the law, so it is offending.

clue.text: Cape supporting antelope

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A headland backing an African antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreland is a cape or headland jutting into the sea.

clue.text: See 7
Footballer's absorbing books on the beach?

indicators.note: the footballer's name takes in the abbreviation for books

parts.note: Pele was the great Brazilian footballer
BB is a common abbreviation for books

explanation.surface: A footballer reading books on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A pebble is a small smooth stone of the kind found on a shingle beach.

clue.text: Something of a paradox? Yes, year and month's about right

annotationWithheld.why: 'Something of a paradox? Yes, year and month's about right': Y + MO(R)ON gives YMORON, but the OX must come from 'paradox' inside the definition (a word doing two jobs); 'Yes' gives no OX
annotationWithheld.clue: Something of a paradox? Yes, year and month's about right

clue.text: From funny setter, witty crossword starts now

indicators.note: the answer is made from the letters of the words that follow

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
the first two letters of crossword

explanation.surface: A setter claims his witty puzzle begins a new era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' signals an anagram of FUNNY SETTER WITTY plus CR, the starting letters of crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: The present day lies in the period after the year 2000, the current hundred years.

clue.text: Long jump by jumper holding false coin

indicators.note: the jumper's word holds the word for false

parts.note: a flea is a jumping insect
lying means false or untruthful
P stands for penny, a coin

explanation.surface: A long jump by an athlete in a sweater clutching a fake coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying leap is a long running jump through the air.

clue.text: Soldier that's dropped gave tongue for few miles in Persia

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier dropped by parachute
to give tongue is to sing out, as hounds do

explanation.surface: A paratrooper sang his way across a few Persian miles.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasang was an old Persian measure of distance, about three and a half miles.

clue.text: Deployed hand 'n' eye to be mother of two queens

indicators.note: the letters are deployed, set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
short for and, giving the letter N
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hand and an eye are put to use by a royal mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Hyde, wife of James II, was mother of Queens Mary II and Anne.

clue.text: See 11
Pawnbroker's cat resident in cabin

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: The pawnbroker's cat lives in a hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Uncle Tom's Cabin lived in that cabin.

clue.text: A good buy, apart from the profit

parts.note: bar means except, apart from
gain is profit

explanation.surface: A good purchase, leaving profit aside.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is something bought cheaply, a good buy.

clue.text: Intend to study the pattern

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a template is a pattern to copy from

explanation.surface: Planning to examine the design.
explanation.definitionFit: To contemplate doing something is to have it in mind as a plan.

clue.text: Word of now stressed importance in bringing up children?

definitions.meaning: a word of honour, a promise given by a prisoner released early

definitions.text: now stressed importance in bringing up children?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., the father's part, now emphasised in child-rearing

explanation.surface: Fathers' part in child-raising is now given weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: split the answer as PA ROLE, a dad's role.
explanation.definitionFit: Parole is a promise on one's honour, and parole itself is French for word.

clue.text: Strikebreaker takes notes on flower

parts.note: a scab is a worker who breaks a strike
IOUs are notes promising payment

explanation.surface: A blackleg takes notes on a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabious is a wild flower with pincushion-like heads, often blue or mauve.

clue.text: See 20
15, half of it in beautiful Devon village

parts.note: the answer to 15 is a hundred years, and C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: the fifty letter goes into the word for beautiful

parts.note: lovely means beautiful
half a hundred is fifty, L in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A hundred-year-old beauty spot in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: C and L are Roman 100 and 50. Clovelly is a picturesque village on the coast of Devon, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Clovelly is a famous steep-streeted fishing village on the north Devon coast.

clue.text: Coloured outside like the pole of ambition?

indicators.note: the colour word sits outside the word for like

parts.note: grey is a colour, so grey-coloured
as means like

explanation.surface: A painted outer coat resembles the slippery pole of ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing the greasy pole' is a British idiom for striving to rise in politics or a career.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial pole of ambition is slippery with grease, hard to climb.

clue.text: Giving makes one out at elbows

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Donating makes a person shabby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out at elbows' is an idiom for ragged or poor; 'out' is the anagram signal for AT ELBOWS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestowal is an act of giving or conferring something.

clue.text: A serious problem for capital, if my second changed sides

indicators.note: the second letter, R for right, switches to the other side, L for left

parts.note: Prague is the Czech capital

explanation.surface: Trouble for the capital if its second letter swapped sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital's second letter R (right) becomes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: A plague is a widespread affliction or scourge, a serious problem.
